target: Spoiler-free historical completion record for the discontinued Japanese GREE social game

areas.name: Archival GREE Route
areas.location_cue: The discontinued Japanese GREE login and application launch screen.
areas.note: Official operation ended in May 2015; this area records provenance rather than pretending the service still works.

levels.1: The first version ran inside Japan's GREE mobile service.
levels.2: Use the June 2011 feature-phone release only through a lawful preserved account or first-party archive.
levels.3: Confirm the application package and account provenance without bypassing authentication. Because the official backend is gone, preserve any owned menus or save data and record the failed service response.

levels.1: A later client added touch controls and profile transfer.
levels.2: The December 2011 smartphone release accepted data transferred from the earlier GREE client.
levels.3: On a lawfully preserved device, document the client version and any transferred profile that still opens locally. Do not overwrite the feature-phone data; the transfer and login servers are no longer available.

levels.1: This completion route depends on infrastructure that no longer exists.
levels.2: The Japanese GREE service operated from June 2011 until May 2015.
levels.3: Treat every server-backed checklist item as historically unavailable on a normal account today. A menu screenshot, redistributed binary, or fan description does not prove a completable authenticated profile.

areas.name: Documented Game Systems
areas.location_cue: The unavailable mission, team, friend, inventory, and item-shop menus.
areas.note: Surviving sources establish these systems but not their exhaustive slot lists or completion thresholds.

levels.1: The central route consisted of numerous social-survival missions.
levels.2: A complete profile would clear every mission offered by the live service.

levels.1: Recovered allies formed teams for later missions.
levels.2: A complete profile would rescue every available ally and fill every team slot.

levels.1: The social layer allowed friends to strengthen difficult attempts.
levels.2: A complete profile would use the friend-cooperation system wherever it tracked progress or rewards.

levels.1: Friends could exchange recovery resources through the service.
levels.2: A complete profile would satisfy every tracked healing-item sharing milestone.

levels.1: The free service also contained a paid item economy.
levels.2: A complete historical profile would own every permanent gameplay item that the catalog offered.

areas.name: Completion Boundary
areas.location_cue: The research record beside any lawfully preserved local client data.
areas.note: The correct result is an explicit unavailable-content record, not a fabricated 100% claim.

levels.1: Mission, roster, shop, and ending totals remain unproven.
levels.2: Do not mark the game complete until an authenticated full catalog or first-party specification is recovered.

levels.1: Server loss is an external boundary, not unfinished local play.
levels.2: Record the title as not achievable on a normal save under current official service conditions.
levels.3: Preserve the eight-source corpus, owned client metadata, and any personal save without attempting unauthorized access. Reopen this checklist only if Capcom or GREE restores authenticated service or releases complete archival data.
